svg.aria-label: Five steps left to right, each shown twice: once as satz commands in a terminal, once as satz studio, the desktop app. Steps 1 to 3 run as the logged-in user with a local state file; steps 4 and 5 run as the IaC service account with the state in the bucket. Step 1, write the estate: satz init with the day-0 values, or satz interview --create, which asks them one at a time; in studio the skeleton is created with that command, opened, and the Interview view asks the day-0 questions. Step 2, bootstrap: satz bootstrap runs the pre-flight on the scope root and the billing account, then creates the folder, project, billing link, APIs and state bucket; studio shows the command line to copy or open in the terminal and never runs it inside the app. Step 3, apply as yourself: transpile, plan, apply as your credentials, which creates the identity layer; studio runs transpile and plan itself and hands apply to the terminal. Step 4, switch to the service account: satz migrate --mode cloud rewrites deployment_mode, migrates the state into the bucket and makes provider and backend impersonate the service account; plan reads No changes and whoami names the account; in studio migrate runs in the terminal and the runs-as chip shows the account. Step 5, add packs one at a time: uncomment a pack's use line or answer its question in satz interview, merge-presets writes the line for a pack the library gained, then transpile, plan and apply per pack; in studio the Map view enables packs and switches, the Interview view asks the questions a pack brings, transpile and plan run in the app and apply in the terminal.

Every step ends with a plan that reads No changes before the next begins. Studio needs satz on the PATH at its minimum version; an older one is refused.
